newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sugar law suit sparked by favouritism - Mackay.
newsitem.headline: Sugar law suit sparked by favouritism - Mackay.

text.p: Legal action being taken against Queensland Sugar Corp was because of its perceived favouritism for other refiners, Mackay Refined Sugars Pty Ltd chief executive officer Jim Hughes told Reuters.
Hughes was responding to questions following Mackay's surprise lodging of a claim for up to A$200 million damages against the QSC.
Apart from Mackay, there are two other major refiners in the Australian market, CSR Ltd and Manildra Harwood.
Mackay's claim had been lodged at the Federal Court on Thursday, Hughes told Reuters.
Discussing background to the claim, the Mackay chief said litigation would not have occurred had the Trade Practices Commission (TPC) allowed Mackay and CSR to merge in 1993.

Mackay Refined Sugars, which after the TPC merger refusal went on to build a sugar refinery in the Queensland city of Mackay in a joint-venture with international commodities group E.D.& F. Man, had been battling ever since.
Ongoing legal action against CSR was scheduled to appear before the court again in a couple of weeks, he said.
This case concerned the use of market power in the price-cutting war in train in the Australian market for years, he said.
